title: Short Stuff: Marrying Up
summary: Short Stuff episode on "marrying up" and the terms for it. The hosts define hypergamy (a woman marrying into higher socioeconomic status), note its history across cultures and the 1881 Panjab Castes book reference, and contrast it with hypogamy (marrying down) and homogamy (marriage between similar statuses). They discuss a study finding the trophy-wife stereotype largely unfounded for couples in their early-to-mid twenties, the finding that educational hypergamy (husband more educated than wife) is linked to higher divorce rates while economic hypergamy is not, and the conclusion that the apparent hypergamy in America and Europe is largely explained by the gender pay gap. Sidebar anecdotes include Married with Children characters, Tommy Lee and Pamela Anderson, and the film Husbands and Wives.

segments.title: Opening banter on marrying up
segments.summary: Josh introduces the idea of marrying up and its misogynistic names such as gold digging and trophy wife, and debates when the trophy wife term was coined.

segments.name: x
segments.title: Defining hypergamy and its history
segments.summary: The hosts define hypergamy as a woman trading looks or other assets for higher socioeconomic status. They describe its historical prevalence, geographic hypergamy (rural to urban moves) per Nicole Constable's work, and the parent-driven marriages described in Panjab Castes by Denzil Ibbetson.

segments.title: Stasis problem and the term hypogamy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how universal hypergamy would leave top women and bottom men without partners, a stasis that some mid-twentieth-century research found in some cultures. They introduce hypogamy, marriage of a lower-status man to a higher-status woman.

segments.title: Homogamy and the trophy wife stereotype
segments.summary: Homogamy, marriage between people of similar status, is presented as the dominant pattern. A study of early-to-mid-twenties couples found the trophy wife stereotype largely unfounded, with examples of celebrity age-gap marriages cited as rare exceptions.

segments.title: Divorce rates by type of hypergamy
segments.summary: Economic hypergamy and homogamy showed no greater divorce rates, while marriages where the husband is more educated than the wife had higher divorce rates. The hosts relate this to Tommy Lee and Pamela Anderson.

segments.title: Gender pay gap, declining hypergamy, and pop culture
segments.summary: The hosts note hypergamy is declining as women increasingly out-earn husbands. The researchers attributed the remaining apparent hypergamy in America and Europe to the gender pay gap. The conversation ends with a discussion of Sydney Pollack's character in Husbands and Wives.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts note that differences in educational attainment are more common in binary and gay couples but not more likely to end in divorce, then sign off.
